abstract: Jiuqu serves as the traditional fermentation starter for Chinese alcoholic beverages, primarily consisting of Daqu , Xiaoqu , and Fuqu . Its diverse flavor characteristics stem from variations in production techniques, raw materials, and environmental conditions. As the key source of flavor compounds in alcoholic beverages, Jiuqu fundamentally determines product quality. However, while the inherent open fermentation process generates flavor complexity, it simultaneously poses significant quality control challenges. To enhance alcoholic product quality and flavor stability, investigation of Jiuqu 's major flavor compounds, their formation pathways, influencing factors, and control strategies is essential. This review summarizes key flavor components across major Jiuqu varieties, identifies their primary source pathways, analyzes critical factors affecting flavor formation, and provides effective flavor regulation approaches. This review establishes a foundation for developing robust quality control measures to ensure consistency in Jiuqu production and improves traditional alcoholic beverage quality, while also providing guidelines for researchers exploring flavor regulatory mechanisms in other fermented foods.

Among these compounds, aldehydes are dominant, including acetaldehyde, isobutyraldehyde, isovaleraldehyde, 2-methylbutyraldehyde, valeraldehyde, hexanal, and nonanal, for a total of 12 types of aldehydes (

Peas contain 2-methyl-3-ethyl pyrazine, 2-methoxy-3-isobutyl pyrazine, and other pyrazines; these pyrazines have an extremely strong nutty aroma and sweet caramel aroma. Peas are also rich in proteins and vitamins, which are the precursors for the formation of the flavor compounds (

6.1.1
Choosing high-quality raw materials to make
Jiuqu
Since the formation potential of
Daqu
flavor compounds depends on the nutritional composition in grains, by regulating the grain matrix for making
Daqu
, researchers intend to overcome constraints of traditional production processes and achieve more efficient, diverse, and consistent
Daqu
fermentation methods. It has been reported that the use of wheat with a high protein content can increase the tetramethylpyrazine content in
MTDQ
because these wheats can be enriched with
Bacillus
(including
Halobacillus
and
Virgibacillus
), which promoted the production of tetramethylpyrazine and pointed a way to improve the content of pyrazine compounds production in
MTDQ
(
Sun et al., 2022
;
Hou et al., 2023
;
Hou et al., 2024
). Mei et al. had analyzed the substrate of raw material for
LTDQ
and found that the protein content of black peas was higher (23.92 g/100 g), followed by hemp peas, and the lowest by white peas (
Mei et al., 2023
). The selection of black peas in the production is conducive to improved flavor quality of the
LTDQ
. Proteins serve as essential nutrients for the fermentation processes involved in
Jiuqu
and Baijiu production. However, excessive protein content can lead to increased formation of fusel oils and accumulation of acidic substances, adversely affecting fermentation (
Han et al., 2017
;
Lu et al., 2025
). Research indicates that high-protein wheat yields 1.5–2 times higher ethyl carbamate (EC) concentrations in the resulting liquor compared to low-protein wheat (
Xue et al., 2023
). Further studies by Hou et al. demonstrated that compared to strong-gluten wheat (crude protein content: >30 %), medium-strong gluten (crude protein content: >28 %) and medium-gluten wheat varieties (crude protein content: >26 %) are more suitable for producing
MTDQ
(
Hou et al., 2023
). Similarly, tannin levels in raw materials must be carefully regulated, as excessively high concentrations can also impede fermentation efficiency (
Han et al., 2017
;
Lu et al., 2025
). For instance, Han et al. compared sorghum varieties with different tannin contents and found that an appropriate tannin concentration promotes the synthesis of esters such as ethyl acetate and ethyl octanoate (
Han et al., 2017
). The study showed that ethyl acetate content peaked at a tannin level of 1.94 %, while a higher tannin content of 2.69 % led to a reduction. The optimal tannin content for brewing sorghum is recommended to be within the range of 1–2 %, which may also serve as a useful reference for selecting raw materials in
Jiuqu
production. Therefore, raw material selection should not rely solely on any single component but must consider a balanced composition of multiple nutrients. It is important to note that specific nutritional requirements may vary depending on the type of
Jiuqu
and the target end product.

1
Introduction
Jiuqu
is a traditional Chinese fermentation starter culture produced through controlled cultivation of microbial communities on grain substrates (typically wheat, barley, or rice), primarily comprising
Daqu
,
Xiaoqu
, and
Fuqu
(
Kang et al., 2022
)
.
Its diverse flavor characteristics stem from variations in production techniques, raw materials, and environmental conditions (
Luo et al., 2024
;
Yang, Fan, & Xu, 2024b
). The production process involves: (i) grain crushing and add moisture, (ii) natural or directed microbial inoculation, (iii) temperature-controlled incubation, and (iv) post-processing including drying and aging (
Kang et al., 2022
;
Pan et al., 2023
;
Wu et al., 2021
). The development of
Jiuqu-making
technology, a seminal advancement in microbial biotechnology, emerged from millennia of empirical optimization in fermentation practice, marking humanity's earliest known transition from passive microbial utilization to active microbial cultivation (
Kang et al., 2022
;
Pan et al., 2023
;
Wu et al., 2021
). Although
Jiuqu
is a natural fermentation process, it can be controlled to capture the desired microorganisms needed for subsequent fermentation, while also obtaining enzymes and flavor compounds, thereby forming a complex fermentation starter. The
Jiuqu
produced via this technology is a composite fermentation starter of enzymes, microorganisms, and flavor compounds, making possible the production of a variety of traditional beverages, including
Huangjiu
and Baijiu (
Jin et al., 2017
). As the fermentation starter for alcoholic beverage production,
Jiuqu
primarily determines product quality through three key mechanisms: (i) Its rich microbial community serves as the primary source of fermentation microorganisms, significantly influencing both the fermentation process and metabolite production; (ii) The abundant enzymatic systems (including amylases, proteases and esterases) play crucial roles in substrate saccharification and utilization; (iii)
Jiuqu
contains a large number of flavor compounds and flavor precursors, some of which can enter the liquor through distillation, while others provide precursors for the formation of flavor compounds. Additionally, the abundant nitrogen and carbon sources in
Jiuqu
provide nutrition for subsequent fermentation (
Kang et al., 2022
;
Tang et al., 2024
). In addition, Chinese fermented alcoholic beverages employ
Jiuqu
as a natural fermentation starter, presenting a distinctive contrast to Western fermentation practices that predominantly utilize isolated enzyme preparations and pure yeast cultures (
Wang, Hao, & Ren, 2023
;
Zhu & Tramper, 2013
).
In recent years, researchers have devoted considerable time and resources to unraveling the mysteries of
Jiuqu
. The microorganisms and flavor compounds of
Jiuqu
were examined using a multi-omics approach, which included macro-genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and flavoromics (
Gan et al., 2019
;
Yang, Fan, & Xu, 2021
;
Kang et al., 2022
). Meanwhile, more researchers have been paying more attention to the study of the flavor profile in
Jiuqu.
However, due to the influence of raw materials, production methods, environment, climate, and other factors, there are variations in the flavor of different types of
Jiuqu
(
Liang et al., 2022
). Typically,
Daqu
contains a greater variety of flavor compounds compared to other types of
Jiuqu
. This is likely attributed to its more intricate production process, higher microbial diversity and longer fermentation period, thereby allowing more time for flavor development (
Sakandar et al., 2020
;
Xia et al., 2023
). The flavor composition of the
Jiuqu
could also be affected by the environment (
Jin et al., 2017
;
Zheng et al., 2011
). For instance, Shi et al. detected the flavor compounds of
HTDQ
in different environments spatial zones during fermentation, specifically the upper, middle, and lower layers of the fermentation room (
Shi et al., 2022
). They found that the environmental heterogeneity of various locations in the
Qu
-room during fermentation resulted in the final production of
Daqu
with three different kinds (white, yellow, and black
Daqu
) (
Shi et al., 2022
).
Currently, regulating the flavor profile in
Jiuqu
to improve the quality of liquor has been the highlight of the research. For example, Ali et al. review a range of the most common and powerful methods, including fortification, bioaugmentation, development of microbial consortia, and omics techniques, to give insight into the latest state of knowledge in this field, including the significance of modified
Daqu
and its influence on the quality of Baijiu (
Ali et al., 2024
). To enhance alcoholic product quality and flavor stability, further summarization of major flavor compounds, their formation pathways, influencing factors, and control strategies is necessary. To understand the advances in the field of
Jiuqu
research, we collected a dataset of all studies in the field over the past decade (2014–2024) using the Web of Science and extracted key terms from the title and abstract fields of the dataset using the VOSviewer software tool (
Van Eck & Waltman, 2010
). Key search terms included
Jiuqu
,
Daqu
,
Xiaoqu
,
Fuqu, Maiqu
and
Hongqu
. The co-occurrence network of key terms related to the
Jiuqu
research is shown in
Fig. 1
b. The data in
Fig. 1
b revealed that there were 89 terms with 3 clusters, 3319 links, and 14,560 total link strengths. These clusters demonstrate the research overview of flavor substance diversity in
Jiuqu
. Additionally, we employed the snowballing method to trace references from key publications and incorporated the most recent studies into our analysis (
Wohlin et al., 2022
).

This review first overviews the production processes, classifications, and flavor profiles of various

It then summarizes key flavor components across major

varieties, identifies their primary sources, analyzes critical factors affecting flavor formation, and proposes effective flavor regulation strategies. The aim of this review is to establish a foundation for developing robust quality control measures to ensure consistency in
Jiuqu
production and enhance traditional alcoholic beverage quality, while also providing guidelines for researchers exploring flavor sources and regulatory mechanisms in other fermented foods.
2
Overview of production processes, classification, and flavor profile of
Jiuqu
As illustrated in
Fig. 2
, the manufacturing processes of different
Jiuqu
varieties demonstrate remarkable specificity in three fundamental aspects: raw material composition, production methodology, and environmental conditions (
Xia et al., 2023
). These differential parameters collectively contribute to the distinct flavor profiles characteristic of each
Jiuqu
type. We have briefly summarized production processes, classification and flavor profile of these
Jiuqu
.
Fig. 2
Ecological characteristics of Chinese
Jiuqu
.

2.1
Daqu
Daqu
is a traditional grain-based fermentation starter primarily made from wheat or barley (sometimes including peas or other grains), widely used in China liquor production (
Fig. 3
). The manufacturing process involves crushing the raw materials, mixing with water, and pressing into brick-shaped form either mechanically or manually. These molded
Daqu
undergo fermentation in
Qu
-room for over one month, followed by a storage period for maturation before use (
Ao et al., 2010
;
Shen et al., 2022
;
Zhang et al., 2012
). The diversity of
Daqu
production methods has led to the development of various
Daqu
types, which are systematically classified through two principal categorization systems. Based on distinctive flavor profiles,
Daqu
is categorized into four primary types: Maotai-flavor
Daqu
, Luzhou-flavor
Daqu
, Fen-flavor
Daqu
, and Mixed-flavor
Daqu
. (
Zheng et al., 2011
). Alternatively, classification according to peak fermentation temperature yields three categories: high-temperature
Daqu
(60–70 °C,
HTDQ
), medium-temperature
Daqu
(50–60 °C,
MTDQ
), and low-temperature
Daqu
(40–50 °C,
LTDQ
) (
Zheng et al., 2011
).
Fig. 3
Geographical distribution of traditional Chinese
Jiuqu.
Fig. 3
The aroma profile of
Daqu
is rich and complex, characterized by a unique foundational “
qu
aroma” that harmonizes multi-layered floral, fruity, and roasted notes (
Hu, Huang, et al., 2021
). This distinctive sensory character arises from a diverse array of volatile compounds, primarily including esters, alcohols, acids, pyrazines, and phenols. Specifically, compounds such as butyl acrylate and (2E)-2-octenal contribute floral and fruity nuances, while tetramethylpyrazine significantly imparts the characteristic roasted and nutty aroma (
Cai et al., 2021
;
Tang et al., 2024
;
Yang, Fu, et al., 2024
). The core “qu aroma” has been attributed to the synergistic effects of several key flavor compounds, including isovaleric acid, 1-hexanol, isovaleraldehyde, 2-octanone, trimethylpyrazine, γ-nonalactone, and 4-vinylguaiacol (
Hu, Huang, et al., 2021
). The flavor characteristics of
Daqu
exhibit spatial heterogeneity, which is fundamentally determined by the production processes (
Chen et al., 2025
;
Mu et al., 2025
;
Zhang et al., 2025
). For example, during the fermentation of
HTDQ
, the combined effects of the two-stage turning process (turning the
Daqu
blocks at day 8 and day 16 of fermentation) and variations in the microenvironment shape unique flavor profiles within the
Daqu
blocks, leading to the formation of white
Qu
, yellow
Qu
, and black
Qu
with distinct flavor characteristics at different spatial positions (
Shi et al., 2022
). This differentiation is closely related to local temperature and humidity gradients (
Shi et al., 2022
). The spatial heterogeneity in
Daqu
fermentation contributes to the diversity of
Daqu
's flavor characteristics, which is beneficial for the production of liquors with different flavor profiles. However, this heterogeneity may also affect the consistency of flavor characteristics across different production batches of
Daqu
, potentially influencing standardized production. Therefore, achieving a balance between flavor diversity and product consistency while preserving the unique flavor characteristics of traditional
Daqu
fermentation is a challenge for the future.
2.2
Xiaoqu
Xiaoqu
represents one of the earliest forms of
Jiuqu
with historical origins dating back to the Zhou Dynasty, which gained widespread application during the Tang Dynasty (618–907 CE) and remains prevalent in southern China's liquor production today (
Fig. 3
). As a crucial fermentation starter,
Xiaoqu
plays dual functional roles in both saccharification and microbial inoculation, making it essential for the production of various Baijiu and
Huangjiu
varieties (
Kang et al., 2021
;
Sakandar et al., 2020
;
Tang et al., 2019
). The manufacturing process utilizes rice (including rice bran), wheat bran, and sorghum as primary substrates, which undergo inoculation with traditional “
Qumu
” starter cultures or defined microbial consortia followed by controlled fermentation at 25–30 °C (
Sakandar et al., 2020
). When compared to
Daqu
,
Xiaoqu
exhibits several distinctive characteristics: lower cultivation temperatures, smaller physical dimensions, reduced microbial diversity, and proportionally smaller usage quantities in liquor production batches (
Kang et al., 2022
;
Su et al., 2020
;
Tong et al., 2024
). These technical specifications contribute to
Xiaoqu
's unique biochemical properties and flavor development patterns in traditional Chinese alcoholic beverages.
Compared to
Daqu
,
Xiaoqu
exhibits relatively mild aromatic characteristics with a less diverse profile of flavor compounds. It contains higher concentrations of volatile compounds such as 1-octen-3-ol, 2,3-butanediol, pHenylacetaldehyde, benzaldehyde, octanoic acid, and nonanoic acid (
Tang et al., 2019
). Among these, 1-octen-3-ol contributes notably to its herbaceous, peppermint-like, and mushroom-like notes (
Tang et al., 2019
;
Zheng et al., 2025
).
Xiaoqu
can be systematically classified based on two fundamental parameters: raw material composition and production methodology. In terms of raw materials,
Xiaoqu
can be categorized into two types, namely, Herbal
Xiaoqu
(with herbs) and White
Xiaoqu
(no herbs)
.
The herbs, including vaob loaf, tangerine peel, and licorice, can reduce undesirable microorganisms, enhance the growth of positive microorganisms, and contribute the unique herbal flavor to the liquor (
Tang et al., 2019
). According to the production method of
Xiaoqu
, it can be categorized into three types, namely, traditional
Xiaoqu
, purebred
Xiaoqu
, and mechanical
Xiaoqu
(
Dong et al., 2020
). Traditional
Xiaoqu
, made by natural inoculation in an open environment, have a lot of microorganisms of both positive and undesirable and result in a low output of liquor when it is used in liquor production. To reduce the influence of undesirable microorganisms, herbs, like vaob loaf, are usually added to the production of traditional
Xiaoqu.
With the advance of technology in microbial culture, purebred
Xiaoqu
is made by inoculating special microorganisms, like Rhizobium. Purebred
Xiaoqu
is extensively employed in liquor fermentation, typically in conjunction with yeasts, and has significantly contributed to improving liquor production output.
With the rapid development of the economy and technological advancements, the Baijiu industry is progressing toward mechanization and intelligence. To further reduce labor costs, a new type of
Xiaoqu
(mechanized
Xiaoqu
, produced using mechanical technology) has been developed (
Hu, Yang, et al., 2021
;
Tong et al., 2024
;
Wang, Li, et al., 2023
). Traditional
Xiaoqu
serves as a microbial starter in conventional production, which relies on natural fermentation (uncontrolled room temperature) and requires substantial manual labor. In contrast, mechanical
Xiaoqu
incorporates wheat bran into the raw materials, resulting in reduced viscosity. In addition, the entire production process is automated, remain untouched by workers, including steaming, cooling, inoculating with starter cultures, mixing, temperature- and humidity-controlled cultivation, mechanical ventilation drying, and storage (
Hu, Yang, et al., 2021
). The mechanization of
Xiaoqu
production represents an advancement over traditional methods. Given its high stability, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, mechanized production is becoming the future trend for both Qu-making and the broader Baijiu industry.
2.3
Fuqu
Fuqu
was invented to save grain, and currently has been one of the most important starters for brewing Baijiu.
Fuqu
were made from brans of grains (steamed wheat husk), which were then inoculated with microorganisms (mainly molds and yeasts
)
and cultured at a certain temperature. In
Fuqu
Baijiu production, molds present in the
Fuqu
first hydrolyze starch from raw materials into fermentable sugars, which are subsequently converted into alcohol by yeast during fermentation. Meanwhile, a lot of flavor compounds were produced by microorganisms through metabolism (
Xia et al., 2023
).
Compared to
Daqu
,
Fuqu
exhibits a milder aromatic profile characterized by a distinct wheat bran note
(Ying et al., 2024)
. Its characteristic flavor is closely associated with the specific microorganisms inoculated during its production. For instance, inoculation with
Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
promotes high yields of tetramethylpyrazine, contributing to baked and roasted aromas (
Zhang et al., 2019
). Additionally, bacterial strains such as
Pseudomonas
sp. YF-58 are capable of producing guaiacol compounds—including guaiacol, 4-vinylguaiacol, 4-methylguaiacol, and 4-ethylguaiacol—which impart spicy and smoky notes to
Fuqu
(
Deng et al., 2024
). This is likely attributed to its single raw material (wheat bran) and lower microbial diversity, which consequently generates fewer aroma compounds during fermentation (
Xia et al., 2023
). However, it enhances raw material utilization, increases yield, and significantly shortens the production cycle (
Zheng & Han, 2016
;
Kang et al., 2022
). In addition,
Fuqu
can be used to brew sesame-flavor Baijiu (SFB) together with
HTDQ
(
Xia et al., 2023
). Compared to
Daqu
Baijiu, the aroma of
Fuqu
Baijiu is usually more moderate, which may be caused by the lesser diversity of microorganisms in
Fuqu
and the shorter fermentation period. Consequently, current researchers are also more concerned about developing functional
Fuqu
(
Ai et al., 2019
;
Sakandar et al., 2020
). For instance, Zhu et al. screened
Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
with high production of tetramethylpyrazine and applied it to the production of functional
Fuqu
(
Zhu et al., 2010
). They found that the application of the functional
Fuqu
significantly increased the contents of tetramethylpyrazine in the SFB. By inoculating the brans with specific microorganisms, it is possible to control the flavor compounds of Baijiu, but excessive use of
Fuqu
may give Baijiu the “bran of grains” flavor and should be controlled.
2.4
Other
Jiuqu
categories
Maiqu
represents one of the earliest traditional fermentation starters for
Huangjiu
production, manufactured through a process involving wheat binding, controlled hydration and precise molding (
Hou et al., 2025
). During fermentation,
Maiqu
develops a wine-like aroma, while the finished product exhibits a fresh and pleasant fragrance. In contrast, poor-quality
Maiqu
may develop a raw and musty odor (
Wang, 2004
). Key aroma compounds, including 1-nonanol, phenethyl alcohol, 2-methylbutanal, isovaleric acid, 2-octanone, guaiacol, 2,3-dimethylpyrazine, 5-ethyl-2,3-dimethylpyrazine, tetramethylpyrazine (TTMP), camphor, and α-terpineol (
Fig. 2
), not only define the characteristic aroma profile of
Maiqu
samples but also serve as key volatile markers for distinguishing between different types of
Maiqu
(
Han et al., 2025
).
Aspergillus, Rhizoctonia
, and
Trichoderma
are the dominant microorganisms in
Maiqu
, which also contains small amounts of bacteria and yeast. These microorganisms provide amylase and protease enzymes, which have the role of hydrolyzing and saccharifying raw materials.
Hongqu
serves as a fundamental fermentation starter for
Huangjiu,
with widespread application in Southeast Asian brewing traditions (
Kang et al., 2022
). It is produced through sequential processing of rice, including immersion, steaming, controlled cooling, and inoculation with
Monascus purpureus
, followed by solid-state fermentation under optimized conditions (
Ai et al., 2019
).
Hongqu
develops distinctive alcoholic and bitter almond aromas during fermentation, contributing to its unique aroma profile (
Lin, 2020
). The resulting
Hongqu
imparts distinctive qualities to
Huangjiu
characterized by vibrant red pigmentation, refined taste profile and complex aromatic bouquet, with Gutian
Hongqu
and Wuyi
Hongqu
recognized as geographical indications of Chinese varieties (
Chen, Li, et al., 2023
;
Lv et al., 2013
). The resulting
Hongqu
imparts distinctive qualities to
Huangjiu
, characterized by vibrant red pigmentation, a refined taste profile, and a complex aromatic bouquet. Gutian
Hongqu
and Wuyi
Hongqu
are recognized as geographical indications of Chinese varieties (
Chen, Li, et al., 2023
;
Lv et al., 2013
). Characteristic flavor compounds identified during the
Huangjiu
brewing process with these two types of
Hongqu
include 3-methylbutan-1-ol, isobutanol, ethyl lactate, ethyl acetate, octanoic acid, diethyl succinate, phenethyl alcohol, hexanoic acid, and n-decanoic acid (
Chen, Yuan, et al., 2023
). However, quality consistency remains challenging due to technological limitations in traditional production methods, high environmental sensitivity during fermentation and incomplete quality standardization systems, prompting current research initiatives focusing on implementing modern fermentation control technologies (
Ai et al., 2019
;
Ma et al., 2022
).

3.1
Esters
Esters, one of the most important flavor compounds of
Jiuqu
, usually have a pleasant aroma profile and confer a degree of health attributes to the food.
Table 1
summarizes the 30 major ester compounds in the different
Jiuqu
. The esters were reported to be higher in
HTDQ
, followed by
MTDQ
, and lowest in
LTDQ
(
Jin et al., 2019
). Ethyl palmitate and methyl linoleate are the main volatile compounds common to all three macrobiotics. From
Table 1
, it can be seen that ethyl palmitate and methyl linoleate are the main volatile compounds common to all three kinds of
Daqu
. In addition, ethyl acetate, ethyl butyrate, and ethyl caproate are also key flavor components of the
Jiuqu
(
Mu et al., 2023
;
Wang et al., 2022
).
The content and type of esters change during the fermentation of the different
Jiuqu.
For instance, Yang et al. detected the flavor compounds of
MTDQ
in different fermentation stage an found that 22 compounds such as ethyl acetate, ethyl butyrate, and ethyl hexanoate showed a tendency of first increasing and then decreasing during the maturation process of
Daqu
(
Yang et al., 2022
). Ethyl valerate, ethyl formate, and ethyl heptanoate were only produced in the middle stage; ethyl isobutyrate and ethyl isovalerate were only produced in the final stage (
Yang et al., 2022
). Yu Mu et al. detected volatile flavor compounds in three different processes of
MTDQ
and found that methyl caproate, methyl oleate, and methyl linoleate accounted for more than 50 % of the flavor compounds in
MTDQ
(
Mu et al., 2023
).The high-content ester of
Jiuqu
was also high in liquor. For instance, ethyl valerate, ethyl caprylate, methyl linoleate, and ethyl hexadecanoate are not only the main flavor compounds in
MTDQ
but also are found at relatively high content in Strong flavor Baijiu (SFB). This suggested there may be a potential association between the flavor compounds of
Jiuqu
and liquor.
3.2
Alcohols
Alcohols are not only the important aroma-presenting compounds in the
Jiuqu
but also the important flavor precursors. During the maturation process of the
Jiuqu
, alcohols react with acids to form esters, which give the
Jiuqu
a certain “wine aroma” (
Yang et al., 2022
). Alcohols typically exhibit low olfactory thresholds (generally <1 ppm) and impart distinctive aromatic notes to
Jiuqu
, including fruity and floral characteristics. Notably, their sensory profiles demonstrate significant concentration-dependent variations. As shown in
Table 1
, the 15 main alcohols are summarized. Among them, 2,3-butanediol (0.095 ppm), isoamyl alcohol (0.004–0.25 ppm), 1-octen-3-ol (0.001–0.0014 ppm), and phenylethanol (0.564–1 ppm) were highly significant aroma compounds in the different
Jiuqu
(
Li et al., 2023
;
Mu et al., 2023
). 2,3-butanediol contributes to the production of fruity and oniony aromas and can be interconverted with ethylene glycol and 2,3-butanedione. Moderate amounts of isoamyl alcohol give a nail oil and floral aroma to
Jiuqu
and contribute to sweetness and set off the ester aroma, but excessive amounts of isoamyl alcohol bring out a pungent flavor and a bitter taste. Isoamyl alcohol significantly contributes to the aroma profiles of
MTDQ
,
LTDQ
, and
Maiqu
, while also serving as an important bittering agent in Maotai flavor Baijiu. 1-octen-3-ol, which has aroma profiles of herbs, lavender, and mushrooms, and phenyl-ethanol, which has aroma profiles of honey, rose, clove, and pungency, contribute significantly to the aroma profiles of different
Jiuqu
. In addition, n-hexanol, heptanol, 1-nonanol, and furfuryl alcohol were also important aroma compounds in the
MTDQ
, and contributed significantly to the fruity, floral, herbaceous, and pungent aromas.

Acids usually have a vinegary and sweaty odor, and a moderate amount of acid makes people feel comfortable, but an excessive amount may bring irritating odors such as acid and fat stink. Acids are also precursors of other flavor compounds, with high content in the earlier stage of
Daqu
and decreasing in later stages (
Wang et al., 2022
). As shown in
Table 1
, nine major acid compounds in different
Jiuqu
were summarized. Among them, 3-methylbutyric acid had ripe fruity, sweaty, and cashew odor characteristics and had additive and folding effects with 3-methylbutanol and 1-octen-3-ol, respectively, which contributed significantly to the aroma profiles of the
MTDQ
and
LTDQ
(
Mu et al., 2023
). Caproic acid has strong fat odor, sweaty odor, and other unpleasant odor characteristics and is an important aroma substance for both
Xiaoqu
and
Maiqu
. 3-methylbutyric acid and caproic acid were higher in
MTDQ
, whereas linoleic acid, stearic acid, arachidic acid, nonanoic acid and other fatty acids were found to be higher in the
Xiaoqu
, which may be related to their respective microbial composition and can impart a vinegary, sour, and fatty flavor to the
Xiaoqu
(
Mo et al., 2010
).

3.5
Ketones
Ketones, which are less numerous in type and content in
Jiuqu
, can be produced by
Bacillus
(
Jiang et al., 2025
). As a multifunctional microorganism,
Bacillus
contributes significantly to brewing through material breakdown, flavor production, and ecosystem regulation. For instance,
Bacillus subtilis
secretes cellulases that demonstrate synergistic effects when combined with ligninolytic enzymes such as laccase. This enzymatic cooperation significantly enhances the depolymerization of lignin, a structurally complex polymer critical for
Jiuqu
quality. The resulting breakdown products serve as precursors for diverse flavor compounds, including various ketones that contribute to the characteristic aroma profile of fermented products.
Bacillus
further enhance flavor compound production through cooperative interactions with other microbiota. Tu et al. investigated the synergistic relationship between
Pediococcus
and
Bacillus
, revealing that the initial fermentation phase is marked by competitive niche partitioning, while later stages demonstrate a clear transition toward mutualistic cooperation (
Tu et al., 2024
). This microbial shift collectively enhances thermal output and accelerates temperature elevation during fermentation. The heating capacity is critical for sustaining the enzymatic activities, Maillard reaction processes, and flavor precursor synthesis required for Baijiu fermentation. In addition, under thermophilic fermentation conditions,
Bacillus
populations served as primary producers of acetoin (buttery notes), pyrazines (roasted aromas), and guaiacol (savory characteristics), with species-specific metabolic pathways generating distinct volatile markers and unique sensory profiles. Zhu et al. identified dual genetic-environmental control of
Bacillus
flavor metabolism (
Zhu et al., 2025
). There were differences in volatile flavor and sensory characteristics between different
Bacillus
species, and the main genes influencing flavor contribution included padC, alsD and acoA/B, etc. (
Zhu et al., 2025
). This study advances comprehension of Bacillus aroma biosynthesis diversity, enabling data-driven strain optimization for industrial fermentation.

Pyrazines
Pyrazines usually have aroma characteristics such as roasted, nutty, burnt, sweet, and chocolate aromas, which can be produced by means of Maillard reaction and metabolism by microorganisms such as

Pyrazines are primarily generated through Maillard reactions (which initially produce aldehydes and ketones before forming pyrazines in later stages) and microbial metabolic pathways. Compared to other flavor compounds, pyrazine formation requires substantially longer reaction times. Furthermore, the characteristic post-storage elevation in pyrazine concentrations likely results from ecological niche differentiation induced by dynamic environmental shifts (including temperature, humidity, pH, and nutrient availability) during the fermentation-to-storage transition, which may drive microbial community reorganization toward pyrazine-producing populations (

Others flavor compounds
Phenols, terpenoids and sulfur-containing compounds also play an important role in the
Jiuqu
flavor profile (
Table 1
). Guaiacol and 4-vinylguaiacol significantly contribute to the smoky aroma and characteristic sauce fragrance in
HTDQ
, with notably higher concentrations observed in premium-quality Daqu (
Tang et al., 2024
;
Zhang et al., 2022
). β-Caryophyllene, exhibiting distinctive clove and pine resin aromatic notes, is consistently detected in both
MTDQ
and
Xiaoqu
(
Mu et al., 2023
;
Tang et al., 2019
)
.
Sulfur compounds are often the source of off-flavors (such as pickle-like odor) in Baijiu. However, the odors of sulfides such as dimethyl trisulfide can be masked by sorghum alcohol solubilizing proteins. For instance, Zhu et al. conducted a comprehensive investigation of kafirin's inhibitory effects on pickle-like (sulfurous off-odors) in Maotai flavor Baijiu through an integrated analytical approach combining instrumental analysis, sensory evaluation, and computational modeling (
Zhu et al., 2023
). They found that after the addition of kafirin, the aroma profile of the pickle-like Maotai flavor Baijiu changed and approached that of the normal Maotai flavor Baijiu. Further analysis demonstrated the formation of kafirin-VSCs complexes through spontaneous molecular interactions that concurrently reduced compound volatility by 22.05 to 64.28 % while increasing odor detection thresholds by 87.29 to 232.57 %. These quantitative changes confirm the dual mechanistic action of kafirin in both physically restricting vapor phase release and perceptually masking sulfurous off-odors through molecular complexation. In conclusion, kafirin exhibited a significant suppressing effect on the pickle-like off-odor of Maotai flavor Baijiu and this effect could be used to reduce the off-odor of Maotai flavor Baijiu and Maotai flavor Baijiu -derived alcoholic beverages (
Zhu et al., 2023
).

The primary sources pathways of flavor compound formation in
Jiuqu
Jiuqu
serves as the primary source of flavor compounds in traditional alcoholic beverages, critically determining final product quality. A comprehensive understanding of its flavor formation mechanisms is essential for targeted metabolic regulation throughout production, particularly given the remarkable diversity of Chinese
Jiuqu
varieties and their distinct brewing processes. Current research classifies flavor compound derivation pathways into three principal domains (
Table 2
): first, intrinsic compounds from raw grains such as terpenes and fatty acids; second, microbially driven biosynthetic processes including esterification reactions, pyruvate metabolism exemplified by the PDC ADH cascade, the Ehrlich pathway converting amino acids to fusel alcohols, and amino acid transamination; third, non enzymatic reactions such as Maillard reactions, caramelization, and oxidative transformations including lipid peroxidation. These pathways collectively establish the biochemical foundation for
Jiuqu
's flavor profile complexity.

4.1
Flavor compounds from grain materials
It is clear that
Jiuqu
is composed of a variety of grain materials, mainly including wheat, barley, peas and sorghum (
Fig. 5
). These grain materials are rich in amylum, protein, lipids, and a variety of flavor compounds, all of which form the essential foundation for the unique aromatic characteristics of
Jiuqu
. For instance, Wanli Qiang et al. analyzed the flavor composition of different varieties of wheat using GC-IMS (
Qiang et al., 2024
). They had obtained 48 VOCs, of which alcohols were the most abundant, followed by aldehydes. And the content of butanol, butyraldehyde, nonanal, ethyl butyrate, ethyl caproate, and limonene was high in all wheats. Barley is also abundant in various aldehyde compounds (
Zhang et al., 2016
). Zhang et al. conducted an in-depth analysis of the aroma components in barley and identified a total of 37 different aroma compounds. Among these compounds, aldehydes are dominant, including acetaldehyde, isobutyraldehyde, isovaleraldehyde, 2-methylbutyraldehyde, valeraldehyde, hexanal, and nonanal, for a total of 12 types of aldehydes (
Zhang et al., 2016
).
